Accordion

Toggle content sections with .accordion. Each item opens independently; opening one closes others by default.

Default behavior
Zaiku is a lightweight CSS framework with server-driven form validation, preloaders, card effects, tabs, progress bars, and more.
Click a header to toggle its content. By default, opening one item closes any other open item.
Yes! Add data-accordion-multiple="true" to the .accordion container.
<h1>Hello World</h1>
<p>This is the code view.</p>
Multiple open items
This item stays open independently of the others.
Open this while item one is still open — both remain visible.
All three can be open at the same time.
Disabled item (unclickable)
This item works normally.
This one works fine too.
Nested accordion

Accordions can be nested inside other accordion items. Each nested accordion works independently.

This is a top-level accordion item.
This parent contains nested accordions below:
Deeply nested content — this item is inside a nested accordion.
Each nested accordion behaves independently from the parent.
Multiple open works on both the parent and nested accordion.

Scrollable content

Add .accordion-scrollable to constrain content height and make it scroll when it overflows.

Borderless accordion

Add .accordion-borderless to remove the outer border and border-radius — keeps only the item divider borders.

Content for item one — no outer border.
Content for item two — only bottom dividers separate the items.
Content for item three — useful inside tab panels, cards, or modals.
Media embed

Add data-zaiku-media with a link to a supported player (YouTube, Vimeo, SoundCloud, Spotify, Twitch). The iframe is created on open and removed on close to stop playback. Enable via Zaiku.init({ accordion: { media: true } }).

Programmatic callbacks

onOpen and onClose callbacks fire when an accordion item opens or closes. Configure them via Zaiku.init({ accordion: { onOpen: fn, onClose: fn } }). Check the console.

Opened and closed events are logged to the console.
Open your devtools console to see the callbacks firing.
